content:
This thread is to continue this discussion from the comments and elsewhere. Let's start with the following comment from one of the files:
"TODO: are there any advantages of using this and not BoundedFiniteSupport? for instance, is
there any operation which preserves BoundedCompactSupport but not BoundedFiniteSupport?
Decide if we want both classes in mathlib or just one of them. If the latter, rewrite all of
Carleson/ToMathlib to use that one class."

Both these classes have their merits. Right now, I'm thinking that in this project it may be fine to just keep both, considering that the blueprint also mixes assumptions and current use more or less matches the blueprint in most cases. It is less clear what the Mathlib version(s) should be.
There is a tradeoff between weakening assumptions and strengthening conclusions, and one wants to resolve this differently in different situations. I think Mathlib should ideally offer several fully developed test function classes (also Schwartz functions, C_0^∞ etc) with usable automation.
Some comments about these two particular classes:

  1. In the context of harmonic analysis, BoundedCompactSupport is slightly more natural, because it preserves several common operations that BoundedFiniteSupport does not, e.g. convolution, fibrewise integration etc. of course when passing to fibers one also has to be careful with a.e. boundedness vs everywhere boundedness, and measurability.
  2. In most practical cases BoundedCompactSupport is strictly stronger, but in full generality, the two classes are incomparable (e.g. consider the reals with counting measure).
  3. FiniteSupport risks confusion with set-theoretic finite support (which appears in many places in mathlib), so proabbly it should get a different name if/when upstreaming. Bounded could be misread as bounded everywhere if it is implemented as a.e. boundedness.
All three comments sound like arguments in favour of having only BoundedCompactSupport, at least for the moment. Or do you know any applications which genuinely require BoundedFiniteSupport?
I'm cautious about adding a typeclass that we don't clearly see a need for. (Plans and refactorings do change, and duplicating most lemmas is a real cost paid now.)

I agree, BoundedCompactSupport is the one to upstream. And we want to refactor the definition to use everywhere boundedness and StronglyMeasurable to make it invariant under the usual constructions. The current version is also a bit unnatural because HasCompactSupport is a pointwise condition (i.e. can be destroyed by a.e. changes), but membership in L∞L^\inftyL∞ only depends on the a.e. equivalence class.
For this project though, I still think it makes sense to keep also BoundedFiniteSupport because the blueprint uses it (in the CZ sections especially).

(Edited) Of course we could change that in the blueprint though; I think there is no mathematical reason that we would need BoundedFiniteSupport in this project (or in most harmonic analysis projects). This could be quite costly in terms of refactoring effort, it's probably not worth doing at this point.

I agree with the points above:

  • BoundedCompactSupport is the definition we want in Mathlib, and we (probably) don't want BoundedFiniteSupport
  • The blueprint could indeed be refactored to only require BoundedCompactSupport. I don't think it's worth the effort (though maybe that is worth a mention in the paper?)

I don't think the HasCompactSupport assumption in BoundedCompactSupport is too unnatural: it's nice for things to be a.e.-invariant, but if we have a canonical value modulo a.e.-equality (in this case: value 0 outside the essential support), then I don't think it hurts much to enforce that canonical value.
Completely agree, upstream only a refactored version of BoundedCompactSupport but keep both for this project. HasCompactSupport is very natural in view of the typical analysis constructions.
